recipes.title: Pesarattu (Green Moong Dosa)
recipes.description: Andhra's protein-rich breakfast crêpe of soaked whole green moong ground with ginger and green chilli — no fermentation needed. Topped with onion, cumin and coriander and served with ginger chutney.

steps.title: Soak the moong
steps.text: Rinse the whole green moong and rice together two or three times. Cover with plenty of water and soak for 6 hours or overnight, until the beans are plump and some skins split.
steps.visual: Whole green moong and a few grains of rice submerged in water in a steel bowl, the dull green beans swollen with a few skins splitting open

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Drain the moong and rice. Grind with the ginger, green chillies, salt and about ¾ cup water to a smooth, pourable batter, slightly thicker than dosa batter. No fermentation is needed.
steps.visual: A steel mixer jar full of smooth, pale-green moong batter flecked with green chilli, a ladle lifting a thick ribbon of batter

steps.title: Mix the topping
steps.text: Toss the finely chopped onion and coriander with the cumin seeds in a small bowl. This is sprinkled over each pesarattu as it cooks.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of finely chopped onion, chopped coriander and cumin seeds mixed together, beside the jar of green batter

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron tawa on medium-high until a sprinkle of water sizzles away instantly. Wipe it with a few drops of oil on a folded cloth or half an onion.
steps.visual: A black cast-iron tawa with a thin sheen of oil, droplets of water dancing and evaporating on its surface

steps.title: Spread and top
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spread it outward in quick circles into a thin 8-inch round. Scatter a spoonful of the onion topping and press it in lightly. Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge.
steps.visual: A thin pale-green moong crêpe spread across the black tawa, scattered with chopped onion, coriander and cumin seeds, oil bubbling at the edges

steps.title: Cook until crisp
steps.text: Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and the edges lift away from the tawa. Flip for 30 seconds if you like the onions lightly browned, then flip back.
steps.visual: The edge of the pesarattu lifted with a flat spatula to show a golden-brown, lacy underside on the black tawa, onions on top just softened

steps.title: Fold and serve
steps.text: Fold in half and serve hot with ginger chutney (allam pachadi) or coconut chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter; it makes about 6 pesarattu, 2 per person.
steps.visual: Two folded golden-green pesarattu on a steel plate with onion flecks showing, a small bowl of brown ginger chutney and a bowl of white coconut chutney beside them

substitutions.note: Leave out the rice for slightly fewer carbs; the pesarattu will be a little softer and less crisp.
Ghee gives a richer, festive flavour, but the dish is then vegetarian rather than vegan.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 1 day in the fridge; it starts to sour after that. Cooked pesarattu is best eaten fresh.
recipes.reheating: Rewarm on a hot tawa for 30 seconds a side.

recipes.title: Gongura Chicken
recipes.description: Andhra's famously tangy chicken curry, cooked down with a paste of sautéed gongura (sorrel) leaves and red chillies until the dark, sour masala clings to the meat.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Wash and drain the chicken. Rub it with the turmeric, half the chilli powder, half the ginger-garlic paste and a little salt. Set aside for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces in a steel bowl smeared with red chilli, yellow turmeric and ginger-garlic paste

steps.title: Sauté the gongura
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a kadai. Fry the dried red chillies and fenugreek seeds for 30 seconds, then add the gongura leaves. Stir on medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the leaves collapse into a soft, dark mass.
steps.visual: Dark olive-green, wilted gongura leaves collapsed into a soft heap with blistered red chillies in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the gongura paste
steps.text: Let the gongura cool for a few minutes, then grind it with the fried chillies to a coarse paste without adding water.
steps.visual: A coarse, dark-green gongura and red chilli paste in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Wipe the kadai and heat the remaining oil. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add cumin and curry leaves, then the onions and green chillies. Fry for 6 to 7 minutes until golden brown.
steps.visual: Golden-brown sliced onions with slit green chillies and crackling curry leaves in oil in the same black kadai

steps.title: Add the masala
steps.text: Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the remaining chilli powder and the coriander powder. Stir for 30 seconds without letting the spices burn.
steps.visual: Browned onions coated in a reddish-brown masala in the kadai, oil starting to shine at the edges

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and toss on high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the pieces turn opaque. Pour in the water, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces simmering in a thin red masala gravy in the covered kadai, lid slightly lifted to show steam

steps.title: Stir in the gongura
steps.text: Add the gongura paste and garam masala. Cook uncovered on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy is thick and oil floats on top. Taste and adjust salt.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces coated in a thick, dark brownish-green gongura masala with oil glistening on the surface in the black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes off the heat so the sourness settles. Serve with hot rice or jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Gongura chicken in a clay bowl, the dark tangy masala clinging to bone-in pieces, fried curry leaves on top and steamed rice alongside

substitutions.note: For gongura mamsam, pressure-cook the mutton with the onion masala for 5 to 6 whistles before stirring in the gongura paste.
If you can't find gongura, use spinach plus 1 tbsp tamarind pulp — tangy, though not quite the same.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the sourness mellows overnight.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan on low heat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Gongura Pachadi
recipes.description: The pride of Andhra — sorrel leaves sautéed and ground with fried red chillies, garlic and roasted spices into a sharp, sour chutney. Mixed into hot rice with a little ghee and eaten with raw onion.

steps.title: Dry the leaves
steps.text: Pluck the gongura leaves and discard the stems. Wash well, drain and spread on a cloth for 15 minutes until there are no water droplets — wet leaves make the pachadi spoil faster.
steps.visual: Fresh gongura leaves with reddish veins spread out to dry on a white cotton cloth

steps.title: Roast the spices
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the coriander seeds, cumin and fenugreek for about 2 minutes until the fenugreek turns reddish-brown. Remove. Add 1 tsp oil and fry the red chillies for 1 minute until crisp. Remove.
steps.visual: Toasted coriander, cumin and reddish fenugreek seeds on a plate beside a pile of crisp, deep-red fried chillies, the empty black kadai behind

steps.title: Sauté the gongura
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the same kadai, add the gongura and cook on medium for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until it wilts completely, darkens and the moisture dries up.
steps.visual: Gongura leaves cooked down to a dark olive-green, jammy mass in the black kadai, no liquid left at the edges

steps.title: Grind coarsely
steps.text: Grind the roasted spices, fried chillies, garlic and salt to a coarse powder. Add the cooled gongura and pulse a few times to a coarse paste — it shouldn't be smooth.
steps.visual: A coarse, dark brownish-green pachadi in a mixer jar with visible red chilli flecks

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil, add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add curry leaves and hing. Pour the hot tempering over the pachadi and mix well.
steps.visual: Sizzling mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil being poured from a small tadka pan over the dark pachadi in a steel bowl

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve a spoonful mixed into hot rice with a little ghee, with sliced raw onion on the side.
steps.visual: A small mound of dark gongura pachadi with mustard seeds and curry leaves on a steel plate beside white rice and raw onion slices

substitutions.note: Groundnut oil is milder; gingelly oil is traditional and helps the pachadi keep longer.
Some Telangana homes use green chillies for a fresher, brighter-tasting pachadi; it keeps for a shorter time.

recipes.storage: Store in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Always use a dry spoon.

recipes.title: Andhra Chicken Fry (Kodi Vepudu)
recipes.description: A fiery, dry Andhra chicken fry: bone-in chicken cooked in its own juices, then roasted with browned onions, red chilli and garam masala until dark and crusty, finished with fried cashews and curry leaves.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Cut the chicken into small curry-cut pieces, wash and drain well. Mix with turmeric, half the chilli powder, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt. Rest for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Small bone-in chicken pieces in a steel bowl coated in a red-orange chilli and turmeric rub

steps.title: Fry the cashews
steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy kadai on medium. Fry the cashews for about 1 minute until golden, then lift them out and keep aside.
steps.visual: Golden cashews being lifted out of shimmering oil with a slotted spoon from a black iron kadai

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: In the same oil, add curry leaves, onion and green chillies. Fry for 6 to 7 minutes until the onions are deep golden.
steps.visual: Deep golden sliced onions, slit green chillies and crisp curry leaves in oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute. Add the remaining chilli powder and the coriander powder and stir for 20 seconds.
steps.visual: Browned onions coated in a thick red masala paste in the kadai, oil bubbling around it

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken, toss well, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, stirring twice. The chicken cooks in its own juices; add 2 tbsp water only if it sticks.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces in a loose red masala with released juices, steam rising as the lid of the black kadai is lifted

steps.title: Roast until dry
steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until all the liquid is gone and the chicken turns dark and crusty.
steps.visual: Dark, dry, crusty chicken pieces with caramelised masala sticking to them in the black kadai, curry leaves darkened

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Sprinkle over the garam masala and lemon juice, return the fried cashews and toss for 1 minute.
steps.visual: Golden cashews tossed through the dark chicken fry in the kadai, a dusting of garam masala on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter coriander leaves and serve hot as a side with rice and rasam or pappu, or with sliced onion and lemon as a starter.
steps.visual: Andhra chicken fry heaped on a steel plate, dark and crusty with cashews, fried curry leaves and fresh coriander, onion rings and a lemon wedge beside it

substitutions.note: Boneless thigh cooks faster — about 8 minutes covered — and has no bone weight.
Leave out the cashews for a lighter, nut-free fry.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a hot pan with a few drops of water, tossing until heated through.

recipes.title: Andhra Kodi Kura (Chicken Curry)
recipes.description: Home-style Andhra chicken curry in a gravy of deeply browned onions, tomato and ground coconut, spiced with whole garam masala and plenty of red chilli. Made for rice.

steps.title: Grind the coconut
steps.text: Grind the grated coconut with ¼ cup water to a smooth paste. Keep aside.
steps.visual: A smooth, creamy white coconut paste in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Fry whole spices
steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy kadai on medium. Add bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom and fry for 20 seconds until fragrant, then add the curry leaves.
steps.visual: Bay leaves, a cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom pods and curry leaves crackling in hot oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Add the onions and green chillies and fry for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown. Well-browned onions give the curry its colour and sweetness.
steps.visual: A heap of deep golden-brown onions with slit green chillies and whole spices in the black kadai

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato is mushy and oil separates.
steps.visual: A thick, glossy red-brown masala of softened tomato and onion in the kadai, oil pooling at the edges

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and salt. Turn the heat up and toss for 5 minutes until the pieces are coated and no longer pink outside.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces coated in red masala being tossed in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces simmering in a thin, bubbling red gravy in the kadai, lid tilted to one side

steps.title: Add coconut paste
steps.text: Stir in the coconut paste and garam masala. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns a rich orange-brown with oil on top.
steps.visual: A thick, rich orange-brown chicken curry gently bubbling in the black kadai, a film of red oil on the surface

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with chopped coriander and serve with hot rice, jonna rotte or chapati.
steps.visual: Andhra chicken curry in a steel bowl with orange-red gravy, chicken pieces and fresh coriander, a plate of white rice beside it

substitutions.note: Ground soaked cashews give a richer, smoother gravy in place of coconut.
Any neutral cooking oil works.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, or freeze for up to a month.
recipes.reheating: Warm on low heat, adding a splash of water if the gravy has thickened.

recipes.title: Gutti Vankaya Kura (Stuffed Brinjal)
recipes.description: Small purple brinjals slit and stuffed with a roasted peanut, chana dal, coriander and red-chilli masala, then slow-cooked with onion and tomato until meltingly soft.

steps.title: Slit the brinjals
steps.text: Wash the brinjals. Make a cross-slit from the bottom up to about three-quarters of the length, keeping the stem end intact. Drop them into salted water to stop browning.
steps.visual: Small glossy purple brinjals with cross-slits at the base, floating in a steel bowl of water

steps.title: Roast the stuffing
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the peanuts for 3 to 4 minutes until spotted. Add chana dal, coriander seeds, cumin and red chillies and roast 2 minutes more until the dal is golden.
steps.visual: Roasted peanuts, golden chana dal, coriander seeds, cumin and red chillies in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Cool, then grind with the garlic, turmeric and salt to a coarse powder. Sprinkle 1 tbsp water and pulse once so the masala clumps when pressed.
steps.visual: A coarse, reddish-brown peanut masala in a mixer jar, clumping together where pressed with a spoon

steps.title: Stuff the brinjals
steps.text: Drain the brinjals. Gently open each one and press in about 1 tbsp of the masala. Keep any leftover masala for the gravy.
steps.visual: Purple brinjals packed with reddish peanut masala lined up on a steel plate, a little masala left in a bowl

steps.title: Sauté onion and tomato
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds, let them pop, then add curry leaves and onion and fry for 4 minutes until soft. Add the tomato and cook 3 minutes until pulpy.
steps.visual: Softened onion and pulpy tomato with mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Cook the brinjals
steps.text: Arrange the stuffed brinjals in a single layer, sprinkle over the leftover masala and add the water. Cover and cook on low for 18 to 20 minutes, turning them gently every 5 minutes, until completely soft.
steps.visual: Stuffed brinjals, skins wrinkled and darkened, nestled in a thick reddish-brown masala in the covered kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Uncover and cook 2 minutes more if the gravy is loose. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice, pappu or jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Soft stuffed brinjals in a thick peanut-red masala in a serving bowl, scattered with fresh coriander

substitutions.note: For a peanut-free stuffing, use roasted sesame with a spoon of dry coconut.
Gingelly oil adds a nutty depth that suits brinjal.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently, covered, with 2 tbsp water so the brinjals don't stick.

recipes.title: Tomato Pappu
recipes.description: Andhra's everyday dal — toor dal cooked soft with plenty of ripe tomatoes and green chillies, mashed smooth and finished with a garlicky ghee tadka. Comfort food with rice.

steps.title: Soak the dal
steps.text: Rinse the toor dal 2 to 3 times until the water runs clearer, then soak in fresh water for 15 minutes. Drain.
steps.visual: Yellow toor dal soaking in water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Put the dal in the pressure cooker with tomatoes, onion, green chillies, turmeric and 2½ cups water. Cook on medium for 3 to 4 whistles, about 12 minutes, then let the pressure drop on its own. In a saucepan, simmer covered for 35 to 40 minutes.
steps.visual: Toor dal, chopped red tomatoes, onion and green chillies in yellow-tinged water inside an open pressure cooker before closing

steps.title: Mash the pappu
steps.text: Open the cooker, add salt and chilli powder and mash well with a wooden masher or whisk until creamy. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, adding hot water for a thick but pourable dal.
steps.visual: Creamy, orange-yellow mashed tomato dal bubbling gently in the open pressure cooker, a wooden masher resting in it

steps.title: Make the tadka
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a small kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add cumin, dried red chillies and garlic. Fry until the garlic is golden, then add curry leaves and hing.
steps.visual: Golden crushed garlic, red chillies, popping mustard seeds and curry leaves sizzling in ghee in a small tadka kadai

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the sizzling tadka into the dal, stir and cover for 1 minute so the flavours steep.
steps.visual: Ghee tadka with red chillies and curry leaves just poured over the orange dal, glistening on the surface

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with rice and a vegetable fry, or with jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Tomato pappu in a steel bowl, orange and creamy with a ghee tadka, red chillies and coriander on top, rice and a fry beside it

substitutions.note: Use groundnut oil for the tadka to make it vegan.
Moong dal cooks faster (2 whistles) and is lighter on the stomach.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; it thickens as it cools.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of hot water, stirring, until pourable again.

recipes.title: Palakura Pappu (Spinach Dal)
recipes.description: Toor dal cooked with a big bunch of spinach, a little tomato, tamarind and green chillies, then mashed and tempered with garlic and red chilli — a staple Telugu lunch dal.

steps.title: Clean the spinach
steps.text: Wash the spinach in 2 to 3 changes of water to remove grit, drain and chop roughly, including tender stems.
steps.visual: A heap of roughly chopped bright-green spinach on a wooden board beside a steel colander

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and 2 cups water for 3 whistles, about 10 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally, then mash lightly.
steps.visual: Soft, mashed yellow toor dal in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Cook the spinach
steps.text: In a kadai, combine the spinach, onion, tomato and green chillies with the tamarind water. Cook on medium for 6 to 7 minutes until the spinach collapses and the tomato softens.
steps.visual: Wilted dark-green spinach with soft tomato, onion and green chillies simmering in a black kadai

steps.title: Combine and mash
steps.text: Add the cooked dal and salt to the spinach. Mash together lightly with a masher, leaving some texture, and simmer for 5 minutes. Add a little hot water if it is too thick.
steps.visual: A thick, speckled green-and-yellow spinach dal bubbling gently in the kadai

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, then cumin, red chillies and garlic; fry until the garlic is golden. Add curry leaves and hing and pour over the dal.
steps.visual: Golden garlic, red chillies and curry leaves sizzling in oil being poured onto the green dal in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with rice and a spoon of ghee, or with rotte, alongside a vegetable fry.
steps.visual: Palakura pappu in a steel bowl, green and creamy with garlic and red chillies on top, white rice and okra fry beside it

substitutions.note: Thotakura (amaranth) is the other classic Andhra choice for this dal.
Stir in lemon juice at the end instead of tamarind for a fresher sourness.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of hot water, stirring well.

recipes.title: Munagaku Pappu (Drumstick-Leaf Dal)
recipes.description: A nourishing Andhra dal of toor dal and tender drumstick (moringa) leaves, wilted in a little oil, soured gently with tamarind and tempered with garlic and dried chillies.

steps.title: Strip the leaves
steps.text: Run your fingers down each drumstick stem to strip off the small leaflets. Discard stems and any yellow leaves, then wash the leaves in a bowl of water and drain.
steps.visual: A pile of tiny, bright-green drumstick leaflets in a steel colander, bare stems pushed aside on the counter

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric, onion, green chillies and 2½ cups water for 3 whistles, about 10 minutes. Let the pressure drop and mash smooth.
steps.visual: Smooth, mashed yellow dal with soft onion pieces in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Wilt the leaves
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a kadai, add the drumstick leaves and stir on medium for 3 to 4 minutes until wilted and darker. Squeeze the soaked tamarind and add its water.
steps.visual: Wilted, deep-green drumstick leaves in a little brown tamarind water in a black kadai

steps.title: Simmer together
steps.text: Pour the mashed dal into the kadai with salt and stir well. Simmer for 5 minutes so the leaves soften fully into the dal.
steps.visual: Yellow dal flecked all over with dark-green drumstick leaves bubbling gently in the kadai

steps.title: Garlic tadka
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin, red chillies and garlic and fry until the garlic is golden. Add curry leaves and hing, then pour over the dal.
steps.visual: A small pan of sizzling golden garlic, red chillies and curry leaves being tipped over the green-flecked dal

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with steamed rice and a little ghee, or with ragi mudde.
steps.visual: Munagaku pappu in a steel bowl, yellow dal speckled with green leaves and topped with garlic tadka, rice on the side

substitutions.note: If moringa leaves aren't available, use about three times the weight of spinach.
Moong dal gives a lighter, quicker-cooking pappu.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a little hot water, stirring.

recipes.title: Andhra Chepala Pulusu (Fish in Tamarind Gravy)
recipes.description: Coastal Andhra's tangy-spicy fish stew: fish steaks simmered in a tamarind, onion and red-chilli gravy and finished with roasted fenugreek powder. It tastes best a few hours after cooking.

steps.title: Marinate the fish
steps.text: Wash the fish steaks in salted water and pat dry. Rub with turmeric, 1 tsp of the chilli powder and a little salt. Set aside for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Seer-fish steaks on a steel plate rubbed with a thin red-and-yellow coat of chilli and turmeric

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes. Squeeze well, strain and keep the thick extract; discard seeds and fibre.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of thick, dark-brown tamarind extract with a strainer of squeezed pulp resting on top

steps.title: Roast the fenugreek
steps.text: Dry-roast half the fenugreek seeds in the kadai on low heat for 1 minute until reddish-brown, then crush to a powder. This is sprinkled in at the end.
steps.visual: A pinch of reddish-brown roasted fenugreek powder in a small stone mortar

steps.title: Temper and fry onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide kadai. Add mustard seeds, then cumin, the rest of the fenugreek and the curry leaves. Add the onions and green chillies and fry for 6 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced onions, slit green chillies and curry leaves with popped mustard seeds in oil in a wide black kadai

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato, the remaining chilli powder and the coriander powder and cook for 5 minutes until mushy.
steps.visual: A thick red onion-tomato masala in the wide kadai with oil glistening at the edges

steps.title: Simmer the pulusu
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind extract with ½ cup more water, the jaggery and remaining salt. Boil, then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until slightly thickened and the raw tamarind smell is gone.
steps.visual: A glossy, dark reddish-brown tamarind gravy bubbling in the wide kadai

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the fish steaks in a single layer. Don't stir — swirl the kadai gently instead. Cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
steps.visual: Seer-fish steaks submerged in thick red-brown pulusu in the wide kadai, oil rising to the surface

steps.title: Finish and rest
steps.text: Sprinkle over the roasted fenugreek powder and coriander leaves and turn off the heat. Cover and rest for 30 minutes so the fish absorbs the gravy.
steps.visual: The kadai of fish pulusu covered with a lid, chopped coriander visible at the edge, resting on a switched-off stove

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with hot rice. It tastes even better reheated the next day.
steps.visual: Andhra fish pulusu in a clay pot, thick red-brown tamarind gravy around whole fish steaks, curry leaves and coriander on top, a mound of rice beside it

substitutions.note: Rohu (bocha) is the budget-friendly freshwater fish many Andhra homes use for pulusu.
Mackerel is cheaper and richer in omega-3; simmer for 8 minutes.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the flavour improves overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat without stirring until just simmering.

recipes.title: Royyala Iguru (Andhra Prawn Masala)
recipes.description: A thick, spicy Andhra prawn masala — prawns cooked in a deeply browned onion-tomato base with red chilli and garam masala until the masala coats them like a glaze.

steps.title: Marinate the prawns
steps.text: Wash the cleaned prawns and drain well. Toss with turmeric, half the chilli powder and a pinch of salt and set aside for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Grey-pink cleaned prawns in a steel bowl tossed with red chilli and turmeric

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add curry leaves, then the onion and green chillies. Fry on medium for 8 minutes until deep golden.
steps.visual: Deep golden chopped onions with green chillies and crisp curry leaves in a black kadai

steps.title: Build the masala
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato, remaining chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.visual: A thick, brick-red onion-tomato masala in the black kadai with oil pooling at the edges

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Add the prawns and toss on high heat for 2 minutes, then cook on medium for 4 to 5 minutes without water. The prawns release their own juices and curl.
steps.visual: Pink, curled prawns in a loose red masala with a little released liquid in the kadai

steps.title: Reduce to a glaze
steps.text: Cook uncovered for 3 to 4 minutes more, stirring, until the liquid is gone and the masala clings to the prawns. Stir in garam masala and crushed pepper. Don't overcook or the prawns turn rubbery.
steps.visual: Prawns coated in a thick, glossy, dark-red masala with no liquid left in the black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with hot rice and rasam, or with chapati.
steps.visual: Royyala iguru in a brass bowl, prawns glazed in dark-red masala with curry leaves and fresh coriander, white rice alongside

substitutions.note: Cleaned squid rings work well; cook just 3 to 4 minutes so they stay tender.
Coconut oil gives a coastal flavour.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat briefly in a pan over medium heat; prolonged reheating toughens prawns.

recipes.title: Kodiguddu Pulusu (Egg Tamarind Curry)
recipes.description: Boiled eggs, blistered in a little spiced oil, then simmered in a sweet-sour Andhra tamarind and onion gravy. A thrifty weeknight favourite with rice.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Cover the eggs with water in a saucepan, bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel and make 2 to 3 shallow slits on each.
steps.visual: Six peeled hard-boiled eggs with shallow slits on a steel plate, the saucepan in the background

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze and strain to get a thick extract.
steps.visual: Dark-brown tamarind extract in a small steel bowl with the squeezed pulp in a strainer

steps.title: Blister the eggs
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp oil in a kadai with a pinch each of turmeric and chilli powder. Add the eggs and roll them around for 2 minutes until the surface blisters and turns orange. Remove.
steps.visual: Boiled eggs with blistered, orange-red spotted surfaces rolling in a little spiced oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Temper and fry onions
steps.text: Add the remaining oil. Add mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek, dried red chillies and curry leaves. Add the onions and green chillies and fry for 6 minutes until light golden.
steps.visual: Light golden sliced onions with green chillies, red chillies and curry leaves in oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Add tomato and spices
steps.text: Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the remaining turmeric and chilli powder, coriander powder and salt.
steps.visual: Soft onion and tomato coated in a red spice paste in the kadai

steps.title: Simmer the pulusu
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind extract and ½ cup water, add the jaggery and bring to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
steps.visual: A glossy, thick reddish-brown tamarind gravy bubbling in the black kadai

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Slip the eggs into the gravy, spoon it over them and simmer for 5 minutes so they soak up the flavour.
steps.visual: Orange-blistered eggs half-submerged in thick tamarind gravy in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with hot rice.
steps.visual: Egg pulusu in a steel bowl, eggs halved to show yellow yolks in the dark tangy gravy, coriander on top, rice beside it

substitutions.note: Leave out the jaggery for slightly fewer carbs; the pulusu will be sharper.
Gingelly oil is common in Andhra pulusu and adds a nutty note.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently on low heat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Andhra Tomato Egg Curry
recipes.description: Eggs cracked straight into a thick, spicy tomato and onion gravy and gently poached until just set — a quick Andhra curry for rice, chapati or jonna rotte.

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and tomatoes and slit the green chillies. Finely chopped tomatoes melt into a smooth gravy.
steps.visual: Finely chopped onion, a large pile of chopped red tomatoes and slit green chillies on a wooden board

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide kadai with a lid. Add cumin and curry leaves, then the onions and green chillies, and fry for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
steps.visual: Soft golden onions with green chillies and curry leaves in oil in a wide black kadai

steps.title: Cook down the tomatoes
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, turmeric and salt, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once or twice, until they break down into a jammy gravy.
steps.visual: Tomatoes collapsed into a thick, jammy red gravy with onions in the wide kadai

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Add chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala and the water. Cook for 3 minutes until the gravy is thick and the oil separates at the edges.
steps.visual: A deep-red, thick tomato gravy with oil shimmering at the edges of the kadai

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.text: Make 6 small wells in the gravy and crack an egg into each. Spoon a little gravy over the whites, cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set — less for soft yolks, more for firm.
steps.visual: Six eggs with set white edges and bright yellow yolks sitting in wells of thick red tomato gravy in the covered wide kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter coriander and serve straight from the pan with rice, chapati or jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Poached eggs nestled in red tomato gravy in the kadai, garnished with chopped coriander, a stack of rotte beside it

substitutions.note: For a vegetarian version, add paneer cubes and simmer 3 minutes instead of poaching eggs.
Any neutral oil works.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; keeps 1 day in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered on low heat with a spoon of water.

recipes.title: Bendakaya Vepudu (Okra Peanut Fry)
recipes.description: Crisp-edged Andhra okra fry: okra stir-fried uncovered until the sliminess cooks off, then tossed with a quick roasted peanut, garlic, cumin and chilli powder.

steps.title: Dry and cut the okra
steps.text: Wash the okra and pat each pod completely dry with a cloth — any moisture makes it slimy. Trim the ends and cut into ½-inch rounds.
steps.visual: Bright-green okra rounds piled on a wooden board, a kitchen towel and trimmed ends beside them

steps.title: Make the peanut powder
steps.text: Dry-roast the peanuts in the kadai on low for 4 to 5 minutes until spotted. Cool, then pulse with garlic, cumin and chilli powder to a coarse powder.
steps.visual: A coarse, reddish peanut-garlic powder in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add urad dal and chana dal and fry until golden, then add curry leaves.
steps.visual: Golden urad and chana dal, popped mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Fry the okra
steps.text: Add the okra and turmeric and spread out. Cook uncovered on medium for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the sliminess is gone and the edges brown. Don't cover and don't add salt yet.
steps.visual: Okra rounds with browned, crisp edges spread across the black kadai, no stickiness visible

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Sprinkle over salt and the peanut powder and toss for 2 minutes on low until the powder toasts and coats the okra.
steps.visual: Crisp okra coated in reddish peanut powder being tossed in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot as a side with pappu, rice and rasam.
steps.visual: Bendakaya fry in a steel bowl, crisp okra coated in peanut powder with curry leaves, beside a bowl of pappu and rice

substitutions.note: Use roasted sesame for a peanut-free version.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; keeps 1 day in the fridge but loses its crispness.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in a hot dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Dondakaya Vepudu (Ivy Gourd Coconut Fry)
recipes.description: Ivy gourd sliced thin and slow-fried until golden and crisp-edged, then tossed with kobbari karam — a roasted dry-coconut, red chilli and garlic powder.

steps.title: Slice the ivy gourd
steps.text: Wash the ivy gourd, trim both ends and slice into thin rounds. Thin, even slices fry crisp instead of steaming.
steps.visual: Thin pale-green ivy gourd rounds with white centres piled on a wooden board

steps.title: Make kobbari karam
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low, roast the red chillies for 1 minute, then the coconut for 1 to 2 minutes until light golden. Cool and grind with garlic, cumin and a pinch of salt to a coarse powder.
steps.visual: A coarse, sandy, orange-red coconut chilli powder in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add urad dal and curry leaves and fry until the dal is golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden urad dal and curry leaves in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Slow-fry
steps.text: Add the ivy gourd and turmeric. Fry uncovered on medium-low for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the slices shrink, turn golden and crisp at the edges. Add the remaining salt halfway.
steps.visual: Shrunken, golden-brown ivy gourd slices with crisp edges spread across the black kadai

steps.title: Toss with karam
steps.text: Sprinkle in the kobbari karam and toss for 2 minutes on low until fragrant.
steps.visual: Golden ivy gourd slices coated in orange-red coconut powder in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with rice and pappu or rasam.
steps.visual: Dondakaya fry heaped in a steel bowl, golden slices dusted with coconut chilli powder and curry leaves, rice and dal beside it

substitutions.note: Swap coconut for roasted peanuts for a karam podi-style fry.
Beans can be cooked the same way when ivy gourd isn't in season.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Warm in a dry pan for 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Cabbage Pesara Pappu Kura
recipes.description: A light Andhra stir-fry of finely shredded cabbage cooked with soaked moong dal, green chilli and ginger and finished with fresh coconut. Ready in 20 minutes once the dal is soaked.

steps.title: Soak the moong dal
steps.text: Rinse the moong dal and soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
steps.visual: Pale-yellow split moong dal soaking in water in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Shred the cabbage
steps.text: Remove the core and shred the cabbage very finely so it cooks quickly and stays crunchy.
steps.visual: A tall heap of finely shredded pale-green cabbage on a wooden board, the core set aside

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add urad dal, chana dal, cumin and red chillies and fry until the dals turn golden. Add curry leaves and hing.
steps.visual: Golden dals, red chillies, cumin and curry leaves crackling in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.text: Add the onion, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 2 minutes until the onion softens.
steps.visual: Softened chopped onion, green chilli and ginger among the tempering in the kadai

steps.title: Cook the moong dal
steps.text: Add the drained moong dal, turmeric and the water. Cover and cook on low for 4 minutes until the dal is just tender but still holds its shape.
steps.visual: Plump yellow moong dal grains with onion and tempering in the kadai, a little steam rising

steps.title: Stir-fry the cabbage
steps.text: Add the cabbage and salt and stir-fry uncovered on medium-high for 6 to 8 minutes until tender-crisp. Don't overcook — it should still be bright.
steps.visual: Wilted but bright pale-green cabbage tossed with yellow moong dal and mustard seeds in the kadai

steps.title: Add coconut
steps.text: Turn off the heat and fold in the grated coconut and coriander.
steps.visual: Fresh white grated coconut and green coriander being folded into the cabbage in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and pappu or as a light side with chapati.
steps.visual: Cabbage pesara pappu kura in a steel bowl, pale-green cabbage with yellow dal, coconut and curry leaves

substitutions.note: Soaked chana dal gives more crunch; soak for 1 hour and cook 2 minutes longer.
Skip the coconut for a lighter version.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes in a hot pan.

recipes.title: Majjiga Pulusu with Okra
recipes.description: Andhra's gentle buttermilk curry: whisked curd simmered with a ground paste of coconut, soaked chana dal, ginger and green chilli, with pan-fried okra and a mustard–red chilli tadka.

steps.title: Soak the chana dal
steps.text: Rinse the chana dal and soak in warm water for 30 minutes so it grinds smooth.
steps.visual: Yellow chana dal soaking in a small steel bowl of water

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Drain the dal and grind with coconut, ginger, green chillies, cumin and coriander seeds and ¼ cup water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, pale cream-green coconut and dal paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the ground paste, turmeric, salt and about 1 cup water until completely smooth with no lumps.
steps.visual: A large steel bowl of smooth, pale-yellow whisked buttermilk mixture, a whisk resting on the rim

steps.title: Fry the okra
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp oil in a kadai and fry the okra on medium for 7 to 8 minutes until lightly browned and no longer sticky.
steps.visual: Okra pieces with lightly browned edges in a little oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Heat gently
steps.text: Turn the heat to low and pour the curd mixture over the okra. Stir continuously for 6 to 8 minutes until it turns frothy and is just about to boil. Don't let it boil hard or the curd will split.
steps.visual: A pale-yellow, frothy buttermilk curry with green okra pieces just beginning to steam in the black kadai

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: In a small pan, heat the remaining oil. Add mustard seeds, fenugreek, red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pour the sizzling tadka over the pulusu. Turn off the heat.
steps.visual: A sizzling tadka of mustard seeds, red chillies and curry leaves landing on the pale-yellow curry in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature with rice and a dry vegetable fry.
steps.visual: Majjiga pulusu in a steel bowl, creamy pale-yellow with okra pieces, red chillies and curry leaves floating on top, rice alongside

substitutions.note: Sorakaya (bottle gourd) is the other classic; boil the cubes in a little water until tender before adding the curd.
Thinned hung curd gives more protein; add extra water to the same consistency.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat, stirring; do not boil.

recipes.title: Andhra Pulihora (Tamarind Rice)
recipes.description: Festival-style Andhra tamarind rice: cooled rice tossed with a thick tamarind–chilli paste, crunchy peanuts and dals, and a roasted sesame-fenugreek powder. Travels well and tastes better after an hour.

steps.title: Cook and cool the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice and pressure-cook with 2½ cups water for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes, so the grains stay separate. Spread on a wide plate, drizzle with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of turmeric and leave to cool.
steps.visual: Cooked white rice spread out on a wide steel plate with a light yellow tinge from turmeric, steam rising

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ¾ cup hot water for 15 minutes. Squeeze and strain to get a thick extract.
steps.visual: A bowl of thick, dark tamarind extract with a strainer of squeezed pulp beside it

steps.title: Roast the sesame powder
steps.text: Dry-roast the sesame seeds and fenugreek in the kadai on low for 2 minutes until the sesame is golden. Grind or pound to a fine powder.
steps.visual: A small heap of fine, beige roasted sesame-fenugreek powder in a mortar

steps.title: Fry the tempering
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds and peanuts and fry for 2 minutes, then add chana dal and urad dal until golden. Add dried and green chillies, curry leaves and hing.
steps.visual: Golden peanuts, chana and urad dal, red and green chillies and curry leaves sizzling in gingelly oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Make the pulusu paste
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind extract with the remaining turmeric, salt and jaggery. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until it reduces to a thick, glossy paste and oil separates.
steps.visual: A thick, glossy, dark-brown tamarind paste with peanuts and chillies in it, oil separating at the edges of the kadai

steps.title: Mix the rice
steps.text: Add the tamarind paste and sesame powder to the cooled rice and mix gently with your fingers or a flat spoon until every grain is coated, without mashing.
steps.visual: Rice on the wide steel plate turned golden-brown and mixed with peanuts, chillies and curry leaves

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and leave for at least 30 minutes so the rice absorbs the tamarind. Pulihora is traditionally made ahead for temple offerings and journeys.
steps.visual: The plate of tamarind rice covered with a steel lid on the counter

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at room temperature with curd or a papad on the side.
steps.visual: Golden-brown pulihora heaped on a banana leaf, studded with peanuts, red chillies and curry leaves, a small bowl of curd beside it

substitutions.note: Cooked foxtail millet makes a good millet pulihora with more fibre.
Cashews give a festive, temple-style finish.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day at room temperature in a cool kitchen, 3 days refrigerated. The tamarind paste alone keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Usually eaten at room temperature; sprinkle with water and microwave briefly if chilled.

recipes.title: Telangana Mutton Curry (Mamsam Kura)
recipes.description: A robust Telangana-style mutton curry: curd-marinated mutton pressure-cooked in a deeply browned onion masala with roasted dry coconut, whole spices and mint.

steps.title: Marinate the mutton
steps.text: Mix the mutton with curd, half the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt. Cover and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
steps.visual: Bone-in mutton pieces coated in a pale-red curd and chilli marinade in a steel bowl

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: Dry-roast the coconut in the open pressure cooker base on low for 2 minutes until golden and fragrant. Tip out, cool and grind with ¼ cup water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: Golden-brown roasted coconut ground to a smooth tan paste in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pressure cooker base. Fry bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and curry leaves for 20 seconds, then add the onions and green chillies. Fry for 10 minutes until deep brown.
steps.visual: Deep-brown fried onions with whole spices and green chillies in the open aluminium pressure cooker

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato, remaining chilli powder and coriander powder and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
steps.visual: A thick, dark red-brown masala with oil separating at the edges of the cooker

steps.title: Sear the mutton
steps.text: Add the mutton with all its marinade. Cook on high for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the meat changes colour and the masala clings to it.
steps.visual: Mutton pieces coated in thick dark masala being stirred in the open cooker

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Stir in the coconut paste, the water and half the mint. Close and cook on medium for 5 to 6 whistles, about 25 minutes, then let the pressure release on its own.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker closed on the stove with its weight hissing and a wisp of steam

steps.title: Finish the gravy
steps.text: Open the cooker, stir in the garam masala and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to the thickness you like. Check that the mutton is soft enough to pull from the bone.
steps.visual: Tender mutton in a thick, glossy dark-brown gravy bubbling in the open cooker, red oil on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter the remaining mint and the coriander. Serve with jonna rotte, rice or bagara rice.
steps.visual: Telangana mutton curry in a clay bowl, dark gravy with tender mutton, fresh mint and coriander on top, jowar rotte stacked beside it

substitutions.note: For a chicken version, skip pressure-cooking and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Use lemon juice in the marinade for a dairy-free curry.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge or 1 month frozen.
recipes.reheating: Reheat on low heat with a splash of water until bubbling.

recipes.title: Jonna Rotte (Jowar Roti)
recipes.description: Soft, hand-patted Telangana flatbread made with jowar flour and hot water — gluten-free, mildly sweet and nutty, and the classic partner for spicy curries and pachadis.

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan.
steps.visual: Water at a rolling boil in a small steel saucepan

steps.title: Scald the flour
steps.text: Put the jowar flour in a wide bowl. Pour in the hot water a little at a time, mixing with a spoon. Cover and leave for 5 minutes — the hot water makes the gluten-free dough pliable.
steps.visual: Off-white jowar flour mixed into shaggy, steaming clumps in a wide steel bowl

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: While still warm, knead with the heel of your palm for 4 to 5 minutes into a smooth dough with no cracks. Wet your hands if it feels dry. Divide into 4 balls.
steps.visual: A smooth, crack-free ball of pale jowar dough and four portioned balls in the steel bowl

steps.title: Pat out
steps.text: Dust the board with flour. Pat one ball with your fingers, turning it as you go, into a 7-inch round. If you're new to this, roll between two sheets of baking paper.
steps.visual: A thin, round jowar rotte being patted out by hand on a flour-dusted wooden board

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Lift the rotte onto a hot tawa. Brush the top all over with water using your fingers. Cook for 1 minute until the underside has light brown spots.
steps.visual: A pale jowar rotte on a hot black tawa, its top glistening with a thin wipe of water

steps.title: Flip and puff
steps.text: Flip and cook for 1 minute, pressing the edges with a folded cloth so it puffs. Or hold it over an open flame for a few seconds with tongs.
steps.visual: A jowar rotte puffing up into a dome on the tawa, brown spots on its surface

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep the rottes wrapped in a cloth as you make the rest. Serve warm with mutton curry, egg curry or gongura pachadi.
steps.visual: A stack of four speckled jowar rottes in a cloth-lined basket beside a bowl of red curry

substitutions.note: Sajja rotte: bajra flour makes a darker, earthier roti by the same method.
Ragi flour works too but the dough is stickier — pat it on baking paper.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within a few hours, wrapped in a cloth. The dough dries quickly, so make it fresh.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa for 20 seconds a side.

recipes.title: Sorakaya Senagapappu Kura (Bottle Gourd with Chana Dal)
recipes.description: A homely Telangana curry of tender bottle gourd and soaked chana dal cooked in a light onion-tomato masala — soft, mildly spiced and very everyday.

steps.title: Soak the dal
steps.text: Rinse the chana dal and soak in water for 1 hour. Drain.
steps.visual: Yellow chana dal soaking in a steel bowl of water

steps.title: Prepare the gourd
steps.text: Peel the bottle gourd, remove the seedy core if it is mature, and cut into ¾-inch cubes. Taste a small piece raw — discard the gourd if it is bitter.
steps.visual: Pale, translucent-green bottle gourd cubes on a wooden board with the peel to one side

steps.title: Temper and sauté
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds and cumin; when they splutter add curry leaves, onion and green chillies and sauté for 4 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Softened onions with green chillies and curry leaves in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Add the masala
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook for 3 minutes until the tomato softens.
steps.visual: A soft, orange-red onion-tomato masala in the black kadai

steps.title: Cook dal and gourd
steps.text: Add the drained dal, the gourd, salt and water. Stir, cover and cook on low for 18 to 20 minutes until the dal is soft but holds its shape and the gourd is translucent.
steps.visual: Translucent bottle gourd cubes and plump chana dal in a light orange gravy in the covered kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander. Serve with rice or jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Sorakaya chana dal curry in a steel bowl, soft gourd and yellow dal in a light gravy, coriander on top

substitutions.note: Ridge gourd (beerakaya) works the same way and cooks a little faster.
Moong dal needs only 20 minutes' soaking and cooks in 10 minutes.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered on low heat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Bagara Baingan
recipes.description: Hyderabad's festive brinjal curry — baby brinjals simmered in a rich, tangy gravy of roasted peanuts, sesame, dry coconut and onion, sharpened with tamarind. A classic partner for biryani.

steps.title: Prepare brinjals and tamarind
steps.text: Slit the brinjals in a cross from the bottom, keeping the stems on, and soak in salted water. Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the extract.
steps.visual: Cross-slit baby brinjals floating in a bowl of water beside a small bowl of soaking tamarind

steps.title: Roast nuts and seeds
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the peanuts for 3 minutes, then add sesame, coconut and cumin and roast for 1 to 2 minutes until the sesame is golden. Tip out.
steps.visual: Golden roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, coconut and cumin on a steel plate beside the black kadai

steps.title: Roast the onion
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp of the oil in the kadai and fry the onion for 6 to 7 minutes until golden brown.
steps.visual: Golden-brown sliced onions in a little oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Grind the roasted nuts and seeds and the onion with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric and ½ cup water into a smooth, thick paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, thick, reddish-brown nutty paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the brinjals
steps.text: Drain and dry the brinjals. Heat 2 tbsp oil in the kadai and fry them for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and they soften partly. Lift out.
steps.visual: Baby brinjals with blistered, wrinkled purple skins being turned in oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Fry the masala
steps.text: In the remaining oil, add mustard seeds, fenugreek and curry leaves. Add the ground paste and fry on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly so it doesn't catch, until it darkens and oil separates.
steps.visual: A thick, dark reddish-brown nut masala with oil seeping out at the edges of the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the tamarind extract, jaggery, salt and water and bring to a boil. Add the brinjals, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until they are soft and the gravy is thick with oil floating on top.
steps.visual: Soft brinjals in a thick, glossy brown gravy with a layer of red oil on the surface in the covered kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and rest 10 minutes before serving with biryani, bagara rice or jonna rotte.
steps.visual: Bagara baingan in a copper handi, whole brinjals in a thick, oily brown gravy, coriander on top and biryani in the background

substitutions.note: Cashews make a milder, creamier salan; also suits peanut allergies.
Omit the jaggery for slightly fewer carbs; the gravy will be sharper.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; it tastes better the next day.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Hyderabadi Egg Curry (Ande ka Salan)
recipes.description: Boiled eggs in a nutty Hyderabadi salan of deeply browned onions, peanuts, sesame and coconut, enriched with curd and soured with a little tamarind.

ingredients.prep: soaked in ¼ cup warm water

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Prick each a few times with a fork so the gravy soaks in. Put the tamarind to soak.
steps.visual: Six peeled boiled eggs pricked with a fork on a steel plate, a small bowl of tamarind soaking beside them

steps.title: Roast and grind
steps.text: Dry-roast the peanuts, sesame and coconut in the kadai on low for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Cool and grind with ½ cup water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, beige-brown peanut-sesame-coconut paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add curry leaves and onions and fry for 10 minutes on medium, stirring, until deep golden brown.
steps.visual: Deep golden-brown onions and curry leaves in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Fry the masala
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder and stir for 1 minute. Add the nut paste and fry on low for 5 minutes until it darkens and oil separates.
steps.visual: A thick, reddish-brown nutty masala with oil pooling at the edges of the kadai

steps.title: Add curd and tamarind
steps.text: Keep the heat low and stir in the whisked curd for 2 minutes so it doesn't split. Add the strained tamarind water, salt and the water and simmer for 8 minutes.
steps.visual: A creamy, orange-brown salan gravy gently simmering in the kadai

steps.title: Simmer the eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs and garam masala and simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the gravy over the eggs, until it is thick enough to coat a spoon.
steps.visual: Whole boiled eggs in a thick, glossy orange-brown gravy with oil on the surface in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and mint. Serve with rice, biryani or chapati.
steps.visual: Hyderabadi egg curry in a copper bowl, halved eggs showing yellow yolks in nutty brown gravy, mint and coriander on top

substitutions.note: Cashews give a richer, milder gravy.
Use coconut milk for a dairy-free salan.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat on low heat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Telangana Kodi Vepudu (Boneless Chicken Fry)
recipes.description: Telangana's pepper-and-coconut chicken fry: boneless thigh roasted with a freshly ground masala of dry coconut, black pepper, fennel and whole spices, finished with mint.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Toss the chicken with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice and salt. Set aside for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Boneless chicken thigh pieces coated in a red-orange marinade in a steel bowl

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the coconut, pepper, fennel, cumin, cloves and cinnamon in the kadai on low for 2 minutes until fragrant and the coconut is light golden. Cool and grind to a fine powder.
steps.visual: A fine, sandy brown pepper-coconut masala powder in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add curry leaves, onion and green chillies and fry for 5 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced onions, green chillies and crisp curry leaves in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and sear on high for 4 to 5 minutes. Cover and cook on medium for 8 minutes until cooked through.
steps.visual: Boneless chicken pieces seared and coated in red masala in the covered black kadai, juices bubbling

steps.title: Roast with masala
steps.text: Uncover, add the coriander powder and the ground pepper-coconut masala and roast for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is dry, dark and well coated.
steps.visual: Dark, dry-roasted chicken pieces coated in brown pepper-coconut masala in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Toss in the torn mint and serve hot as a starter or with rice and dal.
steps.visual: Telangana chicken fry heaped on a steel plate, dark and peppery with curry leaves and fresh mint, onion rings and lemon wedges beside it

substitutions.note: Breast is leaner; reduce covered cooking to 6 minutes so it stays juicy.
Skip the coconut for a sharper, pepper-forward fry.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a hot pan with a few drops of water.

recipes.title: Pachi Pulusu (Raw Tamarind Rasam)
recipes.description: A no-boil Telangana tamarind rasam — thin tamarind water with raw onion, green chilli and a pinch of jaggery, finished with a hot mustard-cumin tadka. Eaten with rice and pappu in summer.

steps.title: Make tamarind water
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes. Squeeze well, strain into a bowl and add the remaining water.
steps.visual: A large steel bowl of thin, amber-brown tamarind water, squeezed pulp in a strainer beside it

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in the jaggery and salt until dissolved. Taste — it should be pleasantly sour with a hint of sweetness.
steps.visual: A spoon stirring jaggery into the amber tamarind water in the steel bowl

steps.title: Add onion and chilli
steps.text: Add the finely chopped onion. Crush the green chillies lightly with your fingers and drop them in with the coriander.
steps.visual: Finely chopped raw onion, crushed green chillies and coriander floating in the tamarind water in the steel bowl

steps.title: Pour the tadka
steps.text: Heat the oil in a small kadai. Add mustard seeds, cumin and red chillies; when they splutter, add curry leaves and hing and pour the sizzling tadka straight into the pulusu.
steps.visual: A sizzling tadka of mustard seeds, red chillies and curry leaves hitting the surface of the tamarind water

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let it stand for 10 minutes so the onion mellows and the flavours blend.
steps.visual: The steel bowl of pachi pulusu resting on the counter, oil droplets and curry leaves floating on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at room temperature, poured over rice with pappu or a dry fry alongside.
steps.visual: Pachi pulusu in a small steel tumbler-bowl with onion and curry leaves visible, beside a plate of rice and yellow pappu

substitutions.note: Leave out the jaggery for a sharper, lower-sugar pulusu.
Sliced shallots are milder and sweeter.

recipes.storage: Best the same day; keeps 1 day in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Not reheated — serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Sarva Pindi (Rice-Flour Pancake)
recipes.description: Telangana's crisp, rustic rice-flour pancake studded with soaked chana dal, peanuts, sesame, onion and curry leaves, pressed by hand into a pan and cooked until golden.

steps.title: Soak the chana dal
steps.text: Rinse the chana dal and soak it in water for 1 hour. Drain well.
steps.visual: Yellow chana dal soaking in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: In a bowl combine the rice flour, soaked dal, peanuts, sesame, onion, green chilli, curry leaves, coriander, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time to make a soft, slightly sticky dough. Divide into 5 portions.
steps.visual: A soft, off-white rice-flour dough speckled with peanuts, chana dal, sesame, onion and green herbs in a steel bowl, divided into five balls

steps.title: Press into the pan
steps.text: Grease a cold, heavy kadai with 1 tsp oil. Place one portion in the centre and press with wet fingers into a thin layer over the base and slightly up the sides. Poke 5 to 6 holes with your finger.
steps.visual: A thin layer of speckled rice dough pressed into the base of a black kadai, five finger holes poked through it

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drop ½ tsp oil into the holes and around the edge. Cover and cook on medium-low for 5 to 6 minutes until the base is golden and crisp.
steps.visual: The pancake in the covered black kadai, oil bubbling in its holes and the edges turning golden

steps.title: Crisp and lift out
steps.text: Uncover and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more to crisp the top. Ease out with a flat spatula. Cool the kadai under running water or wipe with a wet cloth before pressing the next one — dough won't spread in a hot pan.
steps.visual: A round, golden, crisp-edged sarva pindi being lifted out of the black kadai with a spatula, its underside browned

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with tea, a peanut chutney or a spoon of ghee.
steps.visual: A golden, holey sarva pindi broken into wedges on a steel plate, peanuts and curry leaves visible, a cup of tea and a bowl of chutney beside it

substitutions.note: Leave out peanuts and add a little more sesame for a peanut-free version.
Fresh peas are a common winter variation.

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Leftovers keep 1 day in an airtight box.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp on a tawa for 1 to 2 minutes a side.

recipes.title: Bisi Bele Bath
recipes.description: Karnataka's beloved one-pot meal of rice, toor dal and vegetables simmered with tamarind and a freshly roasted spice powder, finished with ghee-fried cashews. Served piping hot, as the name says.

steps.title: Cook rice and dal
steps.text: Rinse the rice and toor dal together. Pressure-cook with turmeric and 4 cups water for 4 to 5 whistles, about 15 minutes, until very soft. Let the pressure drop and mash lightly.
steps.visual: Soft, mushy yellow rice and dal in an open pressure cooker, a ladle mashing it

steps.title: Roast the spice powder
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the chana dal, urad dal, coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek, red chillies, cinnamon and cloves for 4 to 5 minutes until the dals turn golden. Add the coconut for the last minute. Cool and grind to a fine powder.
steps.visual: A fine, brick-red bisi bele bath powder in a mixer jar, roasted whole spices on a plate beside it

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 10 minutes, squeeze and strain.
steps.visual: Thick brown tamarind extract in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: In a large heavy kadai, boil the carrot, beans, peas and onion with 1½ cups water and salt for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
steps.visual: Orange carrot cubes, green beans, peas and onion simmering in water in a large heavy kadai

steps.title: Add tamarind and spice powder
steps.text: Stir in the tamarind extract, jaggery and 3 to 4 tbsp of the spice powder. Simmer for 5 minutes until the raw tamarind smell goes.
steps.visual: Vegetables in a thick, reddish-brown spiced tamarind broth bubbling in the kadai

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the mashed rice and dal and mix well. Add hot water to get a loose, porridge-like consistency — it thickens as it stands. Simmer on low for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch.
steps.visual: A thick, reddish-brown rice and lentil mixture with vegetables bubbling gently in the kadai

steps.title: Ghee tadka
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, fry the cashews until golden, then add curry leaves and hing. Pour over the bisi bele bath and stir.
steps.visual: Golden cashews, curry leaves and mustard seeds in sizzling ghee being poured over the reddish-brown rice in the kadai

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Serve piping hot with a drizzle of ghee, with boondi, papad or potato chips on the side.
steps.visual: Bisi bele bath in a steel bowl, a thick reddish-brown rice-lentil mix with vegetables, ghee-fried cashews and curry leaves on top, papad beside it

substitutions.note: Samai (little millet) makes a popular millet bisi bele bath with more fibre.
Use groundnut oil for the tadka to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; it thickens considerably.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with hot water, stirring, until it loosens again.

recipes.title: Ragi Mudde (Finger Millet Balls)
recipes.description: The everyday staple of rural Karnataka: finger-millet flour cooked into a dense, smooth dough and shaped into balls. Pinched off and swallowed with bassaru, saaru or a spicy curry.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan. Whisk in 1 tbsp of the ragi flour so the water turns slightly thick.
steps.visual: Boiling water in a heavy steel saucepan turning a thin, cloudy brown from a spoonful of ragi flour

steps.title: Add the flour
steps.text: Lower the heat. Tip the remaining flour into the centre as a mound — don't stir yet. Cover and let it steam on low for 3 to 4 minutes.
steps.visual: A mound of dry brown ragi flour sitting in the centre of simmering water in the saucepan

steps.title: Stir hard
steps.text: Using a flat wooden stick (mudde kolu) or the handle of a wooden spoon, stir and mash vigorously for 3 to 5 minutes until there are no dry lumps and the dough comes together smoothly.
steps.visual: A dense, smooth, dark-brown dough being worked with a flat wooden stick in the saucepan

steps.title: Steam again
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 3 minutes more. The dough turns darker and glossy when cooked through.
steps.visual: A glossy, dark-brown mass of cooked ragi dough in the covered saucepan

steps.title: Shape the balls
steps.text: Dip your hands in cold water. Divide the hot dough into 4 and roll each portion on a wet plate into a smooth ball.
steps.visual: Four smooth, dark-brown ragi balls on a wet steel plate, wet hands rolling one of them

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with bassaru, saaru, a chicken curry or a spoon of ghee. Pinch off small pieces, dip in the curry and swallow without chewing, the traditional way.
steps.visual: Two ragi mudde in a steel plate beside a bowl of green bassaru and a scoop of beans palya

substitutions.note: Jowar flour makes a paler, softer mudde by the same method.

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Leftover mudde can be soaked overnight in water and eaten as ambli (fermented porridge) with buttermilk.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 5 minutes to soften.

recipes.title: Ragi Rotti with Dill and Onion
recipes.description: Rustic Karnataka finger-millet flatbread mixed with onion, dill (sabsige soppu), coconut and green chilli, patted by hand straight onto the pan. A hearty, gluten-free breakfast.

steps.title: Chop the greens
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, dill, coriander, green chillies and curry leaves.
steps.visual: Small piles of finely chopped onion, feathery dill, coriander, green chilli and curry leaves on a wooden board

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a bowl mix the ragi flour, chopped greens, coconut, cumin and salt. Add warm water gradually and knead to a soft, non-sticky dough. Divide into 6 balls.
steps.visual: A soft, dark-brown ragi dough flecked with green dill, onion and white coconut in a steel bowl, six balls portioned beside it

steps.title: Pat onto the tawa
steps.text: Grease a cool tawa with a few drops of oil. Place a ball in the centre and pat it out with wet fingers into a 6-inch round. Poke 3 to 4 holes in it.
steps.visual: A thin, round ragi rotti patted out on a cold black tawa, finger marks and three small holes visible

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat. Drizzle ½ tsp oil into the holes and around the edge, cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until firm with brown spots.
steps.visual: A cooked ragi rotti with crisp, browned spots and edges on the black tawa, oil sizzling in its holes

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Cool the tawa under running water or with a wet cloth before patting the next rotti — the dough won't spread on a hot pan. Using two tawas in turn speeds things up.
steps.visual: A stack of three cooked ragi rottis on a plate while the next one is patted out on the cooled tawa

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut chutney, a spoon of butter or ennegai (stuffed brinjal curry). Two rottis per person.
steps.visual: Two ragi rottis with green dill flecks on a steel plate with a bowl of white coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Chopped fenugreek leaves give a slightly bitter, very popular variation.
Jowar flour gives a softer, paler rotti.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; the dough doesn't keep well as the onion releases water.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa for 30 seconds a side.

recipes.title: Akki Rotti (Rice-Flour Flatbread)
recipes.description: Malnad-style rice-flour rotti mixed with grated carrot, coconut, onion, ginger and coriander, pressed thin onto the pan and cooked until crisp-edged and speckled.

ingredients.measure: a little over ¾ cup, hot

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely grate the carrot and chop the onion, ginger, green chillies and coriander.
steps.visual: Finely grated orange carrot, chopped onion, ginger, green chilli and coriander in neat piles on a wooden board

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the rice flour with the vegetables, coconut, cumin and salt. Pour in the hot water a little at a time, mixing with a spoon, then knead to a soft dough. Cover for 5 minutes and divide into 6 balls.
steps.visual: A soft white rice-flour dough speckled with orange carrot, green herbs and coconut in a steel bowl

steps.title: Pat it thin
steps.text: Grease a cool tawa (or a banana leaf or baking paper) with oil. Pat a ball out with wet fingers into a thin 7-inch round. The thinner it is, the crisper the rotti.
steps.visual: A thin, white, carrot-speckled rotti patted out on a cold greased black tawa, fingerprints visible

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat, drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and cover for 2 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until golden spots appear and the edges crisp.
steps.visual: A white akki rotti with golden-brown spots and crisp edges on the black tawa, oil sizzling at its rim

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Cool the tawa under running water or with a damp cloth before each new rotti, so the dough can be patted out.
steps.visual: A stack of golden-spotted akki rottis on a plate beside the cooled tawa

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut chutney, kori gassi or a dollop of butter. Two rottis per person.
steps.visual: Two speckled akki rottis on a banana leaf with a bowl of green coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Grated cucumber (southekai) is another classic Malnad variation; squeeze out excess water.
Ghee gives a richer flavour but makes it vegetarian rather than vegan.

recipes.storage: Best fresh.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa for 30 seconds a side.

recipes.title: Neer Dosa
recipes.description: Mangalore's lacy, paper-thin 'water dosa' from a thin batter of soaked rice and coconut — no fermentation, soft as cloth, and made to soak up kori gassi or fish curry.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice 3 times and soak in plenty of water for 4 hours.
steps.visual: Opaque white rice grains soaking under water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Grind very smooth
steps.text: Drain the rice and grind with the coconut and 1 cup water until completely smooth — rub a drop between your fingers to check there is no grit.
steps.visual: A silky, pure-white rice and coconut batter in a mixer jar

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Pour into a bowl, add salt and about 1¼ cups more water to make a very thin, milk-like batter.
steps.visual: A very thin, milk-white batter in a wide steel bowl, a ladle pouring a watery stream

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick pan or well-seasoned tawa on medium-high and wipe with a little coconut oil.
steps.visual: A heated non-stick pan with a thin sheen of coconut oil

steps.title: Pour the dosa
steps.text: Stir the batter (the rice settles). Pour a ladleful from the edge of the pan inward in a quick circle so it forms a thin, lacy sheet, filling any large gaps. Cover and cook for 1 minute.
steps.visual: A paper-thin, lacy white sheet of batter setting across the pan, tiny holes all over it

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: When the edges lift and the top looks dry (it should not brown), fold the dosa in half and then into quarters. Don't flip it.
steps.visual: A soft, white neer dosa folded into a triangle in the pan, no browning, translucent in places

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stack on a plate without overlapping too much while hot, or they stick. Makes about 12; serve 3 per person warm with kori gassi, fish curry or coconut chutney.
steps.visual: Three folded, lacy white neer dosas on a banana leaf beside a bowl of orange chicken curry

substitutions.note: Coconut is optional — many homes make neer dosa with rice alone for a lighter dosa.
Any neutral oil works for greasing.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 1 day in the fridge; stir and thin with water before using. Cooked dosas are best fresh.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 1 minute or warm covered in a pan.

recipes.title: Mysore Rasam
recipes.description: A rich, fragrant rasam from Mysore, made with toor dal, tomato and a freshly roasted masala of coriander, chana dal, pepper and coconut, tempered in ghee. Sip it or pour over rice.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and 1 cup water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes. Mash until smooth.
steps.visual: Smooth, mashed yellow toor dal in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Roast and grind the masala
steps.text: Heat ½ tsp ghee in a small pan on low. Roast the chana dal, coriander seeds, pepper, cumin and red chillies for 3 minutes until golden and fragrant. Add the coconut for 30 seconds. Grind with ¼ cup water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, orange-red coconut spice paste in a mixer jar, a small pan with a few roasted coriander seeds beside it

steps.title: Simmer tomato and tamarind
steps.text: Squeeze the tamarind and strain its water into a saucepan. Add the tomatoes, salt, jaggery and 1 cup water and boil for 6 to 8 minutes until the tomatoes are soft and the raw tamarind smell is gone.
steps.visual: Soft tomato pieces boiling in a thin, reddish-brown tamarind broth in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Add dal and masala
steps.text: Stir in the mashed dal, the ground masala and 1½ cups water. Heat on low until it rises and turns frothy, about 4 minutes. Don't let rasam boil hard — it loses its aroma.
steps.visual: A frothy, orange-red rasam just rising in the saucepan with foam on the surface

steps.title: Ghee tadka
steps.text: Heat the remaining ghee, add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add curry leaves and hing. Pour into the rasam.
