steps.visual: A ghee tadka of popping mustard seeds and curry leaves being poured into the frothy rasam

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add the coriander, cover for 2 minutes and serve hot with rice and ghee, or in a cup to sip.
steps.visual: Mysore rasam in a steel tumbler and bowl, orange-red and slightly thick, ghee glistening with curry leaves and coriander floating on top

substitutions.note: Coconut oil makes it vegan with a similar richness.
Leave out the jaggery for a sharper rasam.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Heat until just frothy; don't boil.

recipes.title: Hesarubele Kosambari (Moong Dal Salad)
recipes.description: A crunchy Karnataka festival salad of soaked moong dal, cucumber, carrot and fresh coconut, seasoned with lemon and green chilli. No cooking needed beyond an optional tadka.

steps.title: Soak the dal
steps.text: Rinse the moong dal and soak in water for 2 hours, until it can be crushed easily between your fingers but is still crunchy.
steps.visual: Pale-yellow split moong dal soaking in water in a glass bowl

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Finely dice the cucumber, grate the carrot, and chop the green chilli and coriander.
steps.visual: Finely diced green cucumber, grated orange carrot, chopped green chilli and coriander on a wooden board

steps.title: Drain the dal
steps.text: Drain the dal in a sieve and shake well so no water is left — wet dal makes the salad soggy.
steps.visual: Plump, drained moong dal in a steel sieve

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the dal, cucumber, carrot, green chilli, coriander and grated coconut.
steps.visual: A colourful mix of yellow dal, green cucumber, orange carrot and white coconut in a wide steel bowl

steps.title: Optional tadka
steps.text: For the traditional finish, heat the oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add curry leaves and hing and pour over the salad.
steps.visual: A small pan of popping mustard seeds and curry leaves being tipped over the colourful salad

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Just before serving, add the salt and lemon juice and toss. Salt draws water from the cucumber, so add it at the last minute.
steps.visual: Lemon juice being squeezed over the kosambari in the steel bowl, a spoon tossing it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away as a side with a meal, or as a light snack.
steps.visual: Hesarubele kosambari in a small steel bowl, yellow dal with cucumber, carrot, coconut, coriander and mustard seeds, a lemon wedge beside it

substitutions.note: Kadale bele kosambari: soaked chana dal is the other festival classic; soak 3 to 4 hours.
Grated raw mango gives a seasonal summer sourness.

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Without salt and lemon it keeps 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.title: Beans Palya
recipes.description: Finely chopped French beans stir-fried with a mustard and urad dal tempering and finished generously with fresh coconut — the everyday Karnataka vegetable side.

steps.title: Chop the beans
steps.text: Wash, top and tail the beans and chop them finely, about ¼ inch.
steps.visual: A heap of finely chopped bright-green beans on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add urad dal, chana dal and red chillies and fry until golden. Add green chilli, curry leaves and hing.
steps.visual: Golden dals, red and green chillies and curry leaves crackling in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Steam the beans
steps.text: Add the beans, turmeric, salt and the water. Stir, cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 minutes until tender but still bright green.
steps.visual: Bright-green chopped beans steaming in the covered kadai, lid lifted to show them tender

steps.title: Dry off
steps.text: Uncover and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes on medium until any water evaporates.
steps.visual: Dry, glossy green beans with mustard seeds and dal in the kadai, no liquid left

steps.title: Add coconut
steps.text: Turn off the heat and mix in the grated coconut.
steps.visual: Fresh white grated coconut being folded through the green beans in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and saaru, or with chapati.
steps.visual: Beans palya in a steel bowl, finely chopped green beans flecked with white coconut, mustard seeds and curry leaves

substitutions.note: Cabbage palya is made the same way; cook it 2 minutes less.
Halve the coconut for a lighter palya.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes in a hot pan.

recipes.title: Hagalakayi Gojju (Bitter Gourd Gojju)
recipes.description: A sweet, sour and spicy Karnataka bitter-gourd curry: fried bitter gourd simmered in tamarind and jaggery with a roasted sesame, coriander and chilli powder. Even bitter-gourd sceptics come round.

steps.title: Salt the bitter gourd
steps.text: Slice the bitter gourd thinly, scraping out large seeds. Rub with half the salt and the turmeric and leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the bitter juice firmly.
steps.visual: Thin green bitter-gourd slices tinged yellow with turmeric, beads of liquid drawn out, in a steel bowl

steps.title: Make the gojju powder
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the sesame, coriander seeds, urad dal, chana dal, fenugreek and red chillies for 3 to 4 minutes until the dals are golden. Cool and grind to a fine powder.
steps.visual: A fine, reddish-brown roasted spice powder in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes, squeeze and strain.
steps.visual: Thick, dark tamarind water in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Fry the bitter gourd
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing, then the squeezed bitter gourd. Fry on medium for 8 to 10 minutes until browned and crisp at the edges.
steps.visual: Browned, crisp-edged bitter-gourd slices with mustard seeds and curry leaves in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer the gojju
steps.text: Add the tamarind water, jaggery, remaining salt and 2 to 3 tbsp gojju powder. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy and the bitter gourd is coated.
steps.visual: Bitter-gourd slices in a thick, glossy, dark-brown sweet-sour gravy in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature with rice and saaru, or as a relish with chapati.
steps.visual: Hagalakayi gojju in a small steel bowl, dark glossy bitter-gourd pieces with curry leaves, beside a plate of rice

substitutions.note: Bendekai gojju: fried okra works beautifully with the same gravy.
Halve the jaggery to cut sugar; the gojju will taste more bitter and sour.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently, or serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Majjige Huli (Buttermilk Curry with Ash Gourd)
recipes.description: A cooling Karnataka buttermilk curry: soft-cooked ash gourd in whisked curd thickened with a paste of coconut, soaked dals, green chilli and coriander seeds, tempered in coconut oil.

steps.title: Soak the dals
steps.text: Soak the toor dal and chana dal together in warm water for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of toor and chana dal soaking in water

steps.title: Cook the ash gourd
steps.text: Simmer the ash gourd with turmeric, salt and 1 cup water in a saucepan for 8 to 10 minutes until translucent and tender.
steps.visual: Translucent pale-green ash gourd cubes simmering in light yellow water in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Drain the dals and grind with the coconut, green chillies, ginger, coriander seeds, cumin and ¼ cup water to a very smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, pale-green coconut and dal paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer the paste
steps.text: Stir the paste into the ash gourd with ½ cup water and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the raw smell of the dal goes and it thickens slightly.
steps.visual: Ash gourd cubes in a thick, creamy, pale-green coconut gravy bubbling in the saucepan

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Turn the heat to the lowest and stir in the whisked curd. Keep stirring for 2 to 3 minutes just until it steams and starts to froth, then turn off. Boiling will split the curd.
steps.visual: A creamy, pale-yellow buttermilk curry just starting to froth at the edges of the saucepan, ash gourd visible

steps.title: Temper in coconut oil
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the huli.
steps.visual: A coconut-oil tadka of mustard seeds, red chillies and curry leaves landing on the pale-yellow curry

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add the coriander and serve warm with rice and a palya.
steps.visual: Majjige huli in a steel bowl, creamy pale-yellow with ash gourd cubes, curry leaves, red chillies and coriander on top

substitutions.note: Chow chow (seeme badanekai) is the other favourite vegetable for majjige huli.
A ghee tadka gives a richer, temple-style finish.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Warm on the lowest heat, stirring; don't boil.

recipes.title: Bassaru with Dill and Beans
recipes.description: Old Mysore's two-in-one dish: toor dal, beans and dill cooked together, then the drained stock spiced into a thin, fiery saaru while the solids become a dry palya. Classic with ragi mudde.

steps.title: Cook dal and greens
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor dal, beans and dill with turmeric and 4 cups water for 3 whistles, about 10 minutes. Let the pressure drop.
steps.visual: Soft yellow dal with green beans and dark dill in plenty of greenish stock in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through a colander set over a large bowl. Keep the stock for the saaru and the drained dal and vegetables for the palya.
steps.visual: A steel colander of drained dal, beans and dill resting over a bowl of cloudy green-yellow stock

steps.title: Roast the masala
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a kadai on low. Roast the coriander seeds, cumin, pepper and red chillies for 2 minutes. Add half the onion and the garlic and fry for 3 minutes, then the coconut for 30 seconds.
steps.visual: Roasted coriander seeds, red chillies, softened onion, garlic and coconut in the black kadai

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the roasted masala with the tamarind and 2 tbsp of the drained dal and greens to a smooth paste, adding a little stock.
steps.visual: A smooth, brick-red masala paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Boil the saaru
steps.text: Combine the stock, the ground paste and salt in a saucepan and boil for 6 to 8 minutes. It should be thin and fiery.
steps.visual: A thin, brick-red saaru boiling in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Make the palya
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves and the rest of the onion and fry for 2 minutes. Add the drained dal and greens with a pinch of salt and toss for 3 minutes until dry.
steps.visual: A dry, crumbly mix of yellow dal, green beans and dill with mustard seeds and onion in the black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the saaru in bowls with the palya on the side, with ragi mudde or rice.
steps.visual: A bowl of thin red bassaru and a mound of green dal palya beside two dark ragi mudde on a steel plate

substitutions.note: Harive soppu (amaranth) or any local greens make an equally traditional bassaru.
Fresh peas or field beans (avarekalu) are common in winter.

recipes.storage: Keep saaru and palya separately in the fridge for up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Boil the saaru briefly; warm the palya in a pan.

recipes.title: Mangalorean Chicken Ghee Roast
recipes.description: Kundapur's famous chicken ghee roast — chicken cooked down in a fiery, tangy paste of roasted byadgi chillies, coriander, pepper and garlic, then roasted in ghee until glossy and brick red.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the chicken with curd, lemon juice, turmeric and salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces in a pale-yellow curd marinade in a steel bowl

steps.title: Roast the chillies and spices
steps.text: Heat ½ tsp ghee in the kadai on low. Roast the byadgi chillies for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp but not black. Add coriander, cumin, pepper and fenugreek and roast for 1 minute until fragrant.
steps.visual: Crisp, deep-red byadgi chillies with toasted coriander and cumin seeds in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Grind the roasted spices with garlic, tamarind and the water to a very smooth, thick paste.
steps.visual: A thick, smooth, vivid brick-red chilli paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in the kadai. Add the chicken with its marinade and cook on medium for 8 to 10 minutes until mostly cooked and the liquid has reduced. Lift the chicken out and keep the juices.
steps.visual: Pale, part-cooked chicken pieces in reduced juices in the black kadai

steps.title: Roast the paste
steps.text: Add 1 tbsp ghee and the chilli paste to the kadai. Fry on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens and the ghee separates. Stir in the jaggery.
steps.visual: A glossy, deep brick-red paste with ghee pooling around it in the black kadai

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.text: Return the chicken and its juices. Cook on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the masala is thick and clings to every piece.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces thickly coated in glossy red ghee-roast masala in the kadai

steps.title: Finish with ghee
steps.text: Add the remaining ghee and the curry leaves and toss for 1 minute until the leaves crisp.
steps.visual: Crisp curry leaves and a sheen of melted ghee over the brick-red chicken in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with neer dosa, appam or rice.
steps.visual: Chicken ghee roast in a brass bowl, glossy brick-red and dotted with fried curry leaves, folded neer dosas beside it

substitutions.note: Without byadgi chillies, use Kashmiri chilli powder for the same colour and mild heat; roast it for just 20 seconds.
Leave out the jaggery for a slightly sharper finish.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan on low heat with a teaspoon of water.

recipes.title: Kori Gassi (Mangalorean Chicken Curry)
recipes.description: Mangalore's coconut chicken curry — chicken simmered in a smooth gravy of roasted coconut, red chillies and coriander, softened with coconut milk. Traditionally eaten with neer dosa or rotti.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the chicken with turmeric and salt and set aside for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces tinged yellow with turmeric in a steel bowl

steps.title: Roast the masala
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp coconut oil in a kadai on low. Roast the red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, pepper and fenugreek for 2 to 3 minutes. Add garlic for 1 minute, then the coconut, and roast for 4 to 5 minutes until light golden.
steps.visual: Light golden roasted coconut mixed with red chillies and coriander seeds in a black kadai

steps.title: Grind the gravy paste
steps.text: Cool, then grind with the tamarind and ¾ cup water to a very fine paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, rusty-orange coconut masala paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Heat the remaining coconut oil in the kadai. Add curry leaves and onion and fry for 6 to 7 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced onions and curry leaves in coconut oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and cook on high for 5 minutes, stirring, until it turns opaque.
steps.visual: Opaque chicken pieces tossed with golden onions in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer in masala
steps.text: Add the masala paste and the water, stir well, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy thickens.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces simmering in a thick, orange coconut gravy in the covered kadai

steps.title: Add coconut milk
steps.text: Stir in the coconut milk and heat for 3 to 4 minutes without boiling. Taste for salt and rest for 15 minutes before serving.
steps.visual: A creamy, lighter orange chicken curry gently steaming in the kadai, oil beading on the surface

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with neer dosa, akki rotti or rice.
steps.visual: Kori gassi in a clay bowl, creamy orange gravy with chicken pieces and curry leaves, a stack of lacy neer dosa beside it

substitutions.note: Leave out the coconut milk for a thicker, more rustic gassi with less fat.
For motte gassi, simmer boiled eggs in the gravy for 5 minutes.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently on low; don't boil after the coconut milk is in.

recipes.title: Mangalore Mackerel Curry (Bangude Gassi)
recipes.description: A coastal Karnataka mackerel curry in a bright coconut and byadgi-chilli gravy, soured with tamarind and finished with a coconut-oil onion tadka. Simple, everyday and deeply flavoured.

steps.title: Clean the fish
steps.text: Clean the mackerel, cut each into 3 pieces and rub with turmeric and a little salt. Set aside for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Silver-blue mackerel pieces rubbed with turmeric on a steel plate

steps.title: Toast the spices
steps.text: Dry-roast the red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek and pepper in a kadai on low for 2 minutes until fragrant.
steps.visual: Toasted byadgi chillies, coriander seeds and cumin in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Grind the toasted spices with the coconut, tamarind, a few slices of the onion and ¾ cup water to a fine, smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, bright orange-red coconut masala in a mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Pour the paste into the kadai with the remaining water, green chillies, ginger and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until the raw smell goes.
steps.visual: A bright orange-red coconut gravy bubbling in the black kadai with slit green chillies and ginger strips

steps.title: Cook the fish
steps.text: Slide in the mackerel pieces and simmer on low for 8 minutes without stirring — swirl the kadai gently instead — until the fish is cooked.
steps.visual: Mackerel pieces submerged in thick orange-red gravy in the kadai

steps.title: Onion tadka
steps.text: In a small pan heat the coconut oil and fry the remaining onion until golden, then add curry leaves. Pour over the curry and rest for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Golden fried onion and curry leaves in coconut oil being poured over the fish curry

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with boiled red rice, neer dosa or kori rotti.
steps.visual: Bangude gassi in a clay pot, mackerel pieces in a glossy orange-red coconut gravy topped with fried onion and curry leaves, red rice beside it

substitutions.note: Sardines (bhutai) are just as traditional; cook 6 minutes.
Short on time? Use thick coconut milk and grind the spices with just the onion and tamarind.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; it tastes better the next day.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently without stirring until just simmering.

recipes.title: Mangalorean Rava-Fried Pomfret
recipes.description: Whole pomfret marinated in a garlicky red masala, pressed into a crunchy rava and rice-flour crust and shallow-fried on a tawa until crisp — Mangalore's favourite fish fry.

steps.title: Score the fish
steps.text: Wash the pomfret and pat completely dry. Make 2 to 3 diagonal slashes on each side so the masala seeps in.
steps.visual: Two whole silver pomfret with diagonal slashes on a wooden board

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Mix the Kashmiri chilli, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste, adding a few drops of water only if needed.
steps.visual: A thick, glossy deep-red chilli paste in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the masala all over the fish and into the slashes. Leave for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Pomfret fully coated in deep-red masala, the slashes filled with paste, on a steel plate

steps.title: Coat in rava
steps.text: Mix the rava and rice flour with a pinch of salt on a plate. Press each fish firmly into the mixture on both sides so the coating sticks.
steps.visual: Red-marinated pomfret pressed into a gritty white coating of semolina and rice flour on a plate

steps.title: Shallow-fry
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil on a tawa over medium heat. Fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side, drizzling a little oil around the edges, until the crust is golden and crisp and the flesh flakes at the thickest part.
steps.visual: Two pomfret with a golden, crunchy rava crust sizzling in coconut oil on a black tawa

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drain briefly on paper and serve hot with onion rings, lemon wedges and rice with fish curry.
steps.visual: Crisp, golden-red rava-fried pomfret on a banana leaf with onion rings and lemon wedges

substitutions.note: Seer-fish (anjal) steaks are the other Mangalore favourite; fry 3 to 4 minutes a side.
Use only rice flour for a gluten-free crust.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight away. Marinated raw fish keeps 1 day in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in an air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes or on a hot tawa.

recipes.title: Rava Idli
recipes.description: Bengaluru's instant breakfast idli — roasted semolina and curd batter with a ghee tadka of mustard, chana dal, cashews, ginger and carrot, steamed soft and fluffy in 12 minutes.

steps.title: Make the tadka
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add chana dal and cashews and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
steps.visual: Golden cashews and chana dal with mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger in ghee in a black kadai

steps.title: Roast the rava
steps.text: Add the rava and roast on low for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until aromatic but not brown. Stir in the grated carrot for the last minute. Turn off the heat and cool completely.
steps.visual: Pale, roasted semolina mixed with orange carrot, cashews and curry leaves in the kadai

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Tip the cooled rava into a bowl. Add the curd, water, salt and coriander and mix to a thick batter. Rest for 20 minutes so the rava swells.
steps.visual: A thick, creamy rava batter speckled with carrot, cashews and coriander in a steel bowl

steps.title: Get the steamer ready
steps.text: Bring 2 inches of water to a boil in the steamer or pressure cooker (without its weight). Grease the idli moulds with a little ghee.
steps.visual: A greased steel idli stand beside a steamer with water boiling at the bottom

steps.title: Add the baking soda
steps.text: The batter will have thickened — add 2 to 3 tbsp water if needed for a thick, pourable batter. Sprinkle in the baking soda with 1 tsp water and stir gently; it turns light and bubbly.
steps.visual: A light, bubbly, aerated rava batter being folded with a spoon in the steel bowl

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds three-quarters full and steam on medium for 12 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
steps.visual: Puffed, pale rava idlis with carrot flecks and cashews on top in the idli stand inside the open steamer

steps.title: Rest and unmould
steps.text: Let the idlis rest for 4 minutes, then run a wet spoon around each one to unmould.
steps.visual: Rava idlis being lifted out of the moulds with a wet spoon, golden cashews on their tops

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot, 3 per person, with coconut chutney and vegetable sagu, with a spoon of ghee on top if you like.
steps.visual: Three rava idlis on a steel plate with cashews and carrot flecks, a bowl of white coconut chutney and a bowl of yellow sagu beside them

substitutions.note: Use ¾ tsp fruit salt (Eno) in place of baking soda for an even lighter idli; steam immediately after adding.
Leave out the cashews for a nut-free, lighter idli.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; keeps 1 day in the fridge in a covered box.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes to soften.

recipes.title: Vangi Bath (Brinjal Rice)
recipes.description: A Karnataka classic: tender brinjal cooked with tamarind and a freshly roasted vangi bath powder of dals, chillies, cinnamon and dry coconut, then tossed with rice and roasted peanuts.

ingredients.prep: soaked in ¼ cup warm water

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice and pressure-cook with 2¼ cups water for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes, so the grains stay separate. Spread on a plate to cool.
steps.visual: Fluffy white rice spread out to cool on a wide steel plate

steps.title: Roast the vangi bath powder
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the chana dal, urad dal, coriander seeds, red chillies, cinnamon, cloves and fenugreek for 4 minutes until the dals are golden. Add the coconut for 1 minute. Cool and grind to a fine powder.
steps.visual: A fine, rusty-red vangi bath powder in a mixer jar, roasted dals and chillies on a plate beside it

steps.title: Cut the brinjals
steps.text: Cut the brinjals into thin 2-inch strips and keep them in water so they don't darken.
steps.visual: Thin strips of purple-skinned brinjal floating in a bowl of water

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds and peanuts and fry for 2 minutes until the peanuts are crisp, then add curry leaves and hing.
steps.visual: Crisp, golden peanuts, popped mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Cook the brinjal
steps.text: Add the drained brinjal, turmeric and salt. Toss, cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 minutes until soft but still holding their shape.
steps.visual: Soft, yellow-tinged brinjal strips with peanuts and curry leaves in the covered kadai

steps.title: Add the masala
steps.text: Squeeze in the tamarind extract, add the jaggery and 3 tbsp of the vangi bath powder. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and the brinjal is coated.
steps.visual: Brinjal strips coated in a thick, dark reddish-brown masala in the kadai

steps.title: Toss with rice
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold for 2 minutes on low until evenly coated. Add more powder if you like it spicier.
steps.visual: Rice turned a rusty brown and mixed with brinjal strips, peanuts and curry leaves in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter coriander and serve warm with curd or cucumber salad.
steps.visual: Vangi bath heaped on a steel plate, brown spiced rice with soft brinjal and peanuts, coriander on top, a bowl of curd beside it

substitutions.note: Cooked foxtail millet makes a higher-fibre vangi bath.
Cashews are the festive choice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Extra vangi bath powder keeps 1 month in an airtight jar.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and warm in a covered pan or microwave.

recipes.title: Kodava Koli Curry (Coorg Chicken Curry)
recipes.description: Coorg's dark, peppery chicken curry built on a dark-roasted masala of coriander, pepper and coconut, with an onion-ginger-garlic base and a tangy finish of vinegar in place of kachampuli.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the chicken with turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Set aside for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces coated in red chilli and turmeric in a steel bowl

steps.title: Dark-roast the masala
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the coriander seeds, pepper, cumin, mustard seeds, cloves and cinnamon for 5 to 6 minutes until a shade darker and deeply fragrant — this dark roast is the Kodava signature. Add the coconut and roast 2 to 3 minutes until brown. Cool and grind to a fine paste with ¼ cup water.
steps.visual: A dark, coffee-brown roasted spice and coconut paste in a mixer jar, a few dark-roasted coriander seeds on the counter

steps.title: Grind the onion paste
steps.text: Coarsely grind the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies without water.
steps.visual: A coarse, pale onion-ginger-garlic paste flecked with green chilli in a mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the onion paste
steps.text: Heat the oil in the kadai and fry the onion paste on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until golden and dry.
steps.visual: Golden, dry fried onion paste with oil separating in the black kadai

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and cook on high for 5 minutes, stirring, until it is coated and opaque.
steps.visual: Red-coated chicken pieces tossed with golden onion paste in the kadai

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
steps.visual: Chicken simmering in a thin, reddish gravy in the covered kadai

steps.title: Add masala and vinegar
steps.text: Stir in the dark-roasted masala paste and the vinegar. Simmer uncovered for 6 to 8 minutes until the gravy turns thick and almost black-brown.
steps.visual: Chicken in a thick, very dark brown, peppery gravy bubbling in the black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with akki otti, kadambuttu (rice dumplings) or rice.
steps.visual: Kodava chicken curry in a dark clay bowl, glossy near-black gravy around chicken pieces with fresh coriander, rice rotis stacked beside it

substitutions.note: Kachampuli (Coorg vinegar) is traditional; soaked kudampuli or tamarind also give the tang.
For a mutton version, pressure-cook for 5 to 6 whistles before adding the masala.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; it improves overnight.
recipes.reheating: Reheat on low with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Karnataka Tarkari Huli (Vegetable Sambar)
recipes.description: Karnataka's homestyle sambar: toor dal with drumstick and pumpkin, cooked with tamarind and a touch of jaggery in a freshly ground coconut masala. Gently sweet, tangy and aromatic.

ingredients.prep: soaked in ½ cup warm water

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and 2 cups water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes. Mash smooth.
steps.visual: Smooth, mashed yellow toor dal in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Roast and grind the masala
steps.text: Heat ½ tsp oil in a small pan on low. Roast the chana dal, urad dal, coriander seeds, fenugreek and red chillies for 3 minutes until golden; add the coconut for 1 minute. Grind with ½ cup water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, deep orange-red coconut huli masala in a mixer jar

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: In a large saucepan, combine the drumstick and pumpkin with the strained tamarind water, salt, jaggery and 1½ cups water. Boil for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
steps.visual: Drumstick pieces and orange pumpkin cubes boiling in a thin brown tamarind broth in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the mashed dal, the ground masala and enough water for a medium-thick huli. Simmer on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.visual: A thick, orange-red huli with drumsticks and pumpkin gently bubbling in the saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil, add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add curry leaves and hing. Pour into the huli.
steps.visual: A tadka of popping mustard seeds and curry leaves being poured into the orange huli

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add the coriander and serve hot with rice and ghee, or with idli or ragi mudde.
steps.visual: Tarkari huli in a steel bowl, orange-red with drumstick pieces, pumpkin and curry leaves, a plate of rice beside it

substitutions.note: Chow chow (seeme badanekai) is a lower-carb vegetable choice.
Leave out the jaggery for a sharper, less sweet huli.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of water until bubbling.
